{{Short description|German mathematician (1830–1885)}}
'''Alfred Enneper''' (June 14, 1830, [[Barmen]] – March 24, 1885 [[Hanover]]) was a German mathematician. Enneper earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the [[Georg-August-Universität Göttingen]] in 1856, under the supervision of [[Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet]], for his dissertation about [[function (mathematics)|functions]] with [[complex number|complex]] arguments.<ref>{{citation|title=A Comprehensive Treatment of q-Calculus|first=Thomas|last=Ernst|publisher=Springer|year=2012|isbn=9783034804318|page=56|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oBGTUDVyC8cC&pg=PA56}}.</ref><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=59343}}</ref><ref name="aihs">{{citation|title=Archives Internationales D'histoire Des Sciences|volume=118–119|year=1987|page=60|quote=Alfred Enneper (1830-1885; 1859 Dozent and 1870 associate Prof. in Goettingen). Received doctorate 1856 under Dirichlet; Thesis: "Ueber die Funktion π von Gauss mit complexem Argument".}}.</ref> After his [[habilitation]] in 1859 in Göttingen, he was from 1870 on Professor (Extraordinarius) at Göttingen.<ref name="aihs"/>

He studied [[minimal surface]]s and [[Parametrization (geometry)|parametrized]] [[Enneper's minimal surface]]s in 1864. A contemporary of [[Karl Weierstrass]], the two created a whole class of parameterizations, the [[Enneper–Weierstrass parameterization]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://blogs.ams.org/visualinsight/2013/11/01/enneper-surface/|first=John|last=Baez|authorlink=John Baez|series=Visual Insight|title=Enneper surface|date=November 1, 2013|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|contribution=The Weierstrass-Enneper Representations|title=Dynamics at the Horsetooth|volume=4|year=2012|url=http://www.math.colostate.edu/~shipman/47/volume42011/M641_MKilchrist_Packard.pdf|first1=Myla|last1=Kilchrist|first2=Dave|last2=Packard}}.</ref>
